content.text:
Files now open in tabs along the top of the body instead of the slide-out split, and you can have several open at once. It follows the spec I updated last turn.

**How it works now:**
- The tab bar spans the message list's width, so it stops at the referenced spec sidebar while a task runs.
- **Chat** is always the first tab and shows the message list. It can't be closed.
- Each open file gets its own tab with the file name, a dot while it has unsaved changes, and a close button. Hovering shows the file's path.
- Opening a file that isn't open yet adds a tab just after the selected one and selects it. Opening a file that's already open selects its existing tab, and going to a definition there moves the cursor.
- The selected tab's file takes the full width between the tab bar and the chat input. Nothing slides, and there's no split to drag.
- A tab's close button and the editor's own close button both ask first if the file has unsaved changes. Closing the selected tab selects the one to its right, then the one to its left, then Chat.
- Each file keeps its own unsaved changes, cursor and scroll position while another tab is showing. Each project keeps its own tabs and which one was selected when you switch away and back.
- Renaming a file in the tree reopens it at the new path in the same tab, unless it has unsaved changes. Deleting a file closes its tab without asking.

**Code:** most of the change is in `src/prompt_mode.rs`, where I removed the slide-out and split code. In `src/file_view.rs` I made the close action usable from the tab, and added a way to move the cursor in a file that's already open.

**Tests:** I replaced the old slide-out test with `files_open_in_tabs_of_the_body`, which passes. It opens two files and checks:
- the file sits under the tab bar at the bar's full width, with the chat input below it;
- reopening a file selects its existing tab;
- closing tabs selects the right neighbour and ends on Chat.

The rename and delete handling isn't covered by that test.

**Full suite:** 377 passed and 6 failed.
- Four are the ones that already failed before this change: the three code-to-spec handoff tests and `defaults_are_this_repositorys_templates`.
- The other two are `batch_sent_tasks_run_in_order_in_the_other_mode` and `selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached`, which both failed intermittently earlier in this session too. Each passed three times in a row when run alone.

**Not yet:** I haven't run the app itself, so I haven't seen how the tab bar looks or how it scrolls sideways once there are more tabs than fit. There are also no keyboard shortcuts for switching or closing tabs, because the spec doesn't define any.
